title: Norway Moves Toward Formal FIFA Ethics Complaint Over Trump-Balogun Intervention
description_short: Norway Moves Toward Formal FIFA Ethics Complaint Over Trump-Balogun Intervention
description_medium: The Norwegian Football Association supported an ethics complaint against FIFA president Gianni Infantino after FIFA awarded Donald Trump its Peace Prize. The complaint alleged that the award violated FIFA’s political-neutrality rules. Norway’s action concerned the award and Infantino, separate from the FIFA decision about Folarin Balogun’s match ban.
subcategory: FIFA ethics complaint and political neutrality

preserved_fields.title: Norway Moves Toward Formal FIFA Ethics Complaint Over Trump-Balogun Intervention
preserved_fields.description_short: Norway Moves Toward Formal FIFA Ethics Complaint Over Trump-Balogun Intervention
preserved_fields.description_medium: The Norwegian Football Association, led by president Lise Klaveness, moved to formally file a complaint with FIFA's ethics investigators over President Trump's documented role in clearing Folarin Balogun from his mandatory one-game ban. Klaveness stated publicly: "We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process." The complaint follows Belgium's 4-1 elimination of the US — the match at the center of the scandal — and positions Norway as the leading national federation challenging FIFA's capitulation to American presidential pressure.

notes: Reason: The supplied correction context identifies Norway’s letter supporting an ethics complaint against Infantino over FIFA’s Peace Prize for Trump; the AP page returned 403. The Balogun suspension was a separate story, not the subject of this complaint. Proposed correction: retitle around the Infantino complaint and do not connect it to the separate ban decision.
proposed_correction: Norway Supports FIFA Ethics Complaint Concerning Infantino and the FIFA Peace Prize

title: Trump PAC Spends  Million in Donor Funds on Legal Defense

The article examined donor-funded legal expenses. It does not document the 2023 spending total or the Federal Election Commission complaints described in this entry.

preserved_fields.title: Trump PAC Spends  Million in Donor Funds on Legal Defense
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump PAC Spends  Million in Donor Funds on Legal Defense
preserved_fields.description_medium: Federal election records revealed that Donald Trump Save America PAC spent over  million on legal fees in 2023, using donor money raised for political activities to fund his criminal defense. Donors were not informed their contributions would pay Trump attorneys. FEC complaints were filed over the arrangement. Trump various legal entities collectively spent hundreds of millions on lawyers across multiple criminal and civil cases, raising questions about whether his campaign was primarily a legal defense fund.

notes: Reason: The BBC story covers more than $1.12 million in PAC legal fees in 2022, including payments to Alina Habba’s firm; it does not support the supplied 2023 figure, donor-notice claim, or FEC complaints. Proposed correction: provide the relevant 2023 filings and complaint records, or retitle around the 2022 BBC report and restore its verified amount.
proposed_correction: Save America PAC Spent $1.12 Million on Trump’s 2022 Legal Fees

title: Trump Plaza Casino Opens Amid Labor Violations
description_short: Trump Plaza Casino Opens Amid Labor Violations
description_medium: Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino opened in Atlantic City in May 1984. The record’s labor claims concern contractor payment disputes and minority-hiring commitments, but the linked UPI article reports Trump Castle and Trump Plaza bankruptcies in 1992. That later report does not document the casino’s opening conditions or its labor practices.
subcategory: Trump Plaza opening and construction labor

preserved_fields.title: Trump Plaza Casino Opens Amid Labor Violations
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Plaza Casino Opens Amid Labor Violations
preserved_fields.description_medium: Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino opened in Atlantic City in May 1984, but the construction and opening were marred by disputes with contractors and documented labor violations. Multiple contractors filed liens against Trump for unpaid work, a pattern that would repeat across Trump's real estate portfolio throughout the 1980s. The casino was also cited for failing to meet minority hiring commitments. The New Jersey Casino Control Commission repeatedly investigated Trump's properties for labor and regulatory violations during this period.

notes: Reason: The linked UPI article covers 1992 bankruptcies for Trump Castle and Trump Plaza, not the 1984 opening or the labor and minority-hiring claims in the current summary. Proposed correction: source the opening and each labor allegation separately, or retitle around the 1992 bankruptcy report.
proposed_correction: Trump Plaza’s 1984 Opening; Labor Allegations Need a Relevant Source
